properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 is a real declared dependency in this project's lockfile — it is elliptic's hash layer (MD5/SHA-1/SHA-2/RIPEMD-160 streams, HMAC-DRBG for ECDSA nonce generation). This repo's own JS never calls it directly; it ships with the ganache-cli/truffle dev toolchain that signs Ethereum test transactions. Changeable only by swapping the toolchain, not by editing app code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is Ethereum's transaction-signing curve: every tx the truffle/ganache toolchain signs for this project's tests is an ECDSA-secp256k1 signature. The 28 sites are lockfile entries (ethereumjs-util/elliptic/secp256k1 packages). Quantum-unsafe, but fixed by the Ethereum protocol (ecrecover precompile) — this project can observe, not replace; migration is a chain-level decision. Dev/test toolchain, not a production runtime.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 13 sites are the real `evp_bytestokey` npm package (^1.0.0/^1.0.3) declared in package-lock.json — root entry, a ganache-cli-nested copy, and several transitive dependency blocks. It is a genuine implementation of OpenSSL's deprecated single-round MD5 EVP_BytesToKey key-derivation routine, shipped as part of the crypto-browserify stack that truffle/ganache-cli pull in. No first-party import exists (verified: zero mentions outside the lockfile) — available in the shipped library; use, if any,

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 5 sites are the `bcrypt-pbkdf` package (^1.0.0) plus its nested tweetnacl copy — the OpenBSD bcrypt_pbkdf key-derivation scheme. It ships as a transitive dependency via sshpk (encrypted OpenSSH private-key support) inside the truffle toolchain. No first-party import found; presence in the shipped dependency tree is the inventory fact. Note: the collector's label says "bcrypt password hashing" — the actual package is bcrypt-pbkdf, the bcrypt-based KDF variant — same bcrypt-family primitive, s

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 is pinned at package-lock.json:18209 (verified; marked "optional": true in the lockfile) and genuinely provides RSA keygen/encrypt/sign. Transitive dependency of the truffle toolchain; no first-party import (zero mentions outside the lockfile). The 0.10.0 release (2020) predates the 1.x line; whatever the toolchain uses it for, the build ships an RSA implementation. Observable here, replaceable only by upgrading the toolchain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 6 sites are the `create-ecdh` package (^4.0.0) — the crypto-browserify ECDH component implementing elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman over the elliptic library's curves (including secp256k1/curve25519). Declared in the lockfile at root and as a transitive dependency; also a nested bn.js copy at :8628. Pulled in by the truffle/ganache/web3 toolchain. No first-party call site found; the algorithms ship with the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl provides Ed25519 signing, and two copies are pinned in the lockfile: root node_modules/tweetnacl 1.0.3 (package-lock.json:23494, verified) and a nested 0.14.5 under bcrypt-pbkdf (:7216) — the version the dep_scan label names. Carrier: sshpk's OpenSSH ed25519-key support inside the truffle toolchain. No first-party import; the capability ships with the build. Classical signature — deadline-class PQ risk, migration on the toolchain vendor's schedule.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 provides the ECDSA implementation the Ethereum JS toolchain uses for transaction signing. Declared in the lockfile the build installs; the project's own code has no direct call site (web3/ganache use it under the hood). Same secp256k1 ECDSA family as ALG-673c8f24 — quantum-unsafe signature, fixed by the Ethereum chain protocol.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl's crypto_box/crypto_scalarmult is X25519 (Curve25519) Diffie-Hellman; the same two lockfile copies (1.0.3 root at :23494, 0.14.5 nested under bcrypt-pbkdf at :7216) carry it. Transitive toolchain dependency via sshpk; no first-party call site. Key-agreement class — the retroactively-breakable ("harvest now, decrypt later") risk class, though no first-party traffic uses it here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak/SHA-3 in the Ethereum toolchain's tree (js-sha3, @ethersproject/keccak256) — keccak256 is Ethereum's standard hash for addresses and transaction hashes. Quantum-safe hash family; on Ethereum its use is fixed by chain convention, not by this project. All 33 sites are lockfile dependency declarations in the dev toolchain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The pbkdf2/@types/pbkdf2 entries sit inside ganache-cli's transitive tree — PBKDF2 is one of the two KDFs of the web3 secret-storage (encrypted JSON keystore) spec. The project's own code has no direct PBKDF2 call site. Dev toolchain dependency; the KDF parameters (iterations) live inside the ganache/web3 packages, not in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 26 sites are scrypt-js (2.0.4 and 3.0.x) and scrypt-async (^2.0.1) declared in the lockfile, nested under @ethersproject/json-wallets, web3-eth-accounts, ethereum-cryptography and ganache-cli. These are the scrypt KDFs of the Ethereum keystore format (Web3 Secret Storage v3) — the toolchain uses them to encrypt/decrypt JSON wallet files. Transitive dependencies of the truffle/ganache/web3 stack; no first-party call site. Memory-hard password KDF — adequate margin against Grover.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 (pinned at package-lock.json:18209, "optional": true) provides AES (CBC/CTR/GCM modes) alongside its RSA/X.509 surface. Transitive dependency of the truffle toolchain; no first-party call site found. Symmetric cipher with adequate PQ margin at standard key sizes; the inventory fact is that the build ships it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl's secretbox/box authenticated encryption is XSalsa20-Poly1305; carried by the same two lockfile copies (1.0.3 root, 0.14.5 nested under bcrypt-pbkdf). Symmetric AE with a 256-bit key — PQ-adequate (Grover halves to ~128-bit), which is why the rating is A+. Transitive toolchain dependency; no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 is pinned at package-lock.json:18209 (verified; "optional": true). It is the provider of the RSA, AES and X.509 objects (ALG-589856a1, ALG-0eb2c0da, ALG-1847d707) and also implements TLS 1.2. Transitive dependency of the truffle toolchain; no first-party import found anywhere in the repo. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 provides X.509 certificate parsing/creation/verification (forge.pki). Same carrier as the RSA and AES objects; pinned at package-lock.json:18209. Transitive toolchain dependency; no first-party certificate handling exists in the repo's own code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is the scrypt KDF of the web3 secret-storage keystore spec, declared in the lockfile inside the ganache-cli toolchain tree. No direct call site in the project's own code. Dev/test tooling only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.11 provides SHA-1/SHA-2 stream hashing for the Ethereum JS toolchain (elliptic/ethereumjs use it for key material and DRBG inputs). Declared dependency the build installs; no direct call site in the project's own code.
